tweet.text:
Qwen just made frontier-style reasoning fit in your pocket.

A new 2B distilled Qwen3.8 model takes reasoning traces from the 2.4T flagship and compresses that capability into a model that can run locally on phones and tiny devices.

The crazy part is the size:

Q4_K_M: ~1.3GB

Yet it supports:

→ 262K context
→ Real chain-of-thought reasoning
→ Function calling
→ Full-parameter SFT
→ Teacher-generated reasoning traces
→ No LoRA shortcut
→ Same reasoning curriculum used for the larger 4B/9B models

And the benchmark jump is huge:

MMLU CoT: 28.3 → 54.8
GSM8K: 33 → 64

The important idea here isn’t just “2B model runs on a phone.”

It’s distillation at this scale actually transferring reasoning behavior from a 2.4T teacher into a tiny model.

If the quality holds up outside benchmarks, we’re getting dangerously close to a world where you don’t need a cloud model for a lot of everyday reasoning.

2B parameters. ~1.3GB. 262K context. Runs locally.

quote.text:
FREE GPU. Qwen3.8-27B multimodal from a single Colab T4.

You don’t need a 24GB GPU sitting at home.

This setup runs a 3.7 bpw Ridge GGUF of Qwen3.8-27B on a 16GB T4, while keeping the model’s sensitive Gated-DeltaNet layers protected.

The stack gives you:

→ Qwen3.8-27B multimodal
→ Image understanding
→ Medical-document extraction
→ 3.7 bpw Ridge GGUF
→ Runs on a free Colab T4
→ Full vision support
→ OpenAI-compatible API
→ Your own subdomain
→ Cloudflare Tunnel for a public endpoint
→ Everything inside a single Colab notebook

The clever part is the quantization strategy.

Instead of blindly compressing every layer, Ridge preserves the Gated-DeltaNet components that are more sensitive to quantization while aggressively shrinking the rest of the model.

So a 27B multimodal model can squeeze into a 16GB T4 and expose an API you can connect to your own apps, agents, or tools.

Free cloud GPU + multimodal Qwen3.8 + public API endpoint is a pretty ridiculous combination. https://x.com/0x0SojalSec/status/2092352689745387645/video/1
